analytical_semantics_hardening_8b2.negative_gradient_identity: V(x) = -lambda * grad(C0(x)), proven synthetically (never over the real corpus) via single-source cardinal cases and multi-source metric finite-difference cross-checks on real WGS84 geodesics
analytical_semantics_hardening_8b2.gradient_sign_statement: V points down the C0 gradient (away from sources, toward decreasing C0); positive grad(C0) points toward sources (increasing C0); the two are exactly 180 degrees apart whenever the gradient magnitude is materially nonzero; V is never described as direction of increasing risk or predicted/validated spread direction

cell_local_correction_8b3.arrival_bearing_formula: (az21 + 180) mod 360, where az21 is pyproj.Geod.inv's back azimuth (measured at the cell, pointing back toward the source)

historical_8b_vs_active_8b3_diff_audit.large_bearing_delta_explanation: The bearing-delta maximum (25.4 degrees) occurs exclusively in near-cancellation (low-clarity, near-zero-magnitude) cells, where bearing is inherently ill-conditioned under any small perturbation -- confirmed by the resultant-component delta staying small throughout (max 0.018) and by a synthetic reproduction (a ~0.0006-magnitude perturbation applied to a ~0.0011-magnitude near-cancellation vector reproduces an ~19-degree bearing swing). This is expected angular-statistics behavior near a magnitude singularity, not a geometric defect in either method.

cell_local_correction_8b3.finite_difference_convergence: error shrinks ~100x per 10x step reduction (O(step^2) central-difference truncation) from step=0.1km to step=0.001km, converging to <1e-5 relative error -- proving the corrected identity holds to convergent numerical precision, unlike the historical field's persistent ~2e-4 to 7e-4 relative plateau that never shrank with step size
